title: GOP House member on ’embarrassing’ South Carolina prospects: ‘Darline is dragging Rs’
content: A House Republican described the competitive South Carolina Senate race as “embarrassing,” saying incumbent Sen. Darline Graham (R) is “dragging Rs down the ticket.” He noted Republicans originally won the seat by 18 points and added that the closeness now requires the speaker to travel to South Carolina to help the Republican candidate finish the race.
summary: A House Republican called the competitive South Carolina Senate race “embarrassing” and said incumbent Sen. Darline Graham (R) is “dragging Rs down the ticket.” He noted Republicans won the seat by 18 points and that the speaker must come to South Carolina’s 1st district to pull the Republican across the finish line.
author: The Hill

title: Federal Reserve keeps rates at 3.75%‑4% as inflation linked to energy costs
content: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, holding it in the 3.75 percent to 4 percent range at its most recent policy meeting. Analysts noted that the latest inflation surge appears to stem chiefly from higher energy costs rather than from broad‑based economic pressure.
summary: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates between 3.75 percent and 4 percent at its recent meeting. Analysis suggested that recent inflation was driven mainly by energy costs rather than broad economic pressure.
author: The Hill

title: Charlamagne criticizes Nicki Minaj for targeting Kathy Hochul but not Trump
content: Charlamagne criticized Nicki Minaj for condemning New York Governor Kathy Hochul while not applying the same criticism to former President Donald Trump. The commentary notes that Minaj is entitled to her political views, but argues that moral authority calls for consistent scrutiny of both opponents and those she supports.
summary: Charlamagne criticized Nicki Minaj for condemning Kathy Hochul while not condemning Trump. He said Minaj is entitled to her politics but should apply the same moral scrutiny to the people she supports.
author: The Hill

title: Obamacare premiums on Healthcare.gov to rise double digits in 2027
content: A report published Friday by health research group KFF indicates that Obamacare enrollees could face a 13 % increase in health insurance premiums in 2027, following a 26 % rise from 2025 to 2026. This marks the second consecutive year of double‑digit premium increases.
summary: A report by health research group KFF projects the average cost of Obamacare health insurance on Healthcare.gov will increase 13 percent in 2027. That would represent a double‑digit premium increase for a second year after a 26 percent rise from 2025 to 2026.
author: The Hill

title: Judge Trina Thompson blocks DOJ threat to California election officials over noncitizen voting
content: A California federal judge issued a temporary restraining order on Friday that bars the Department of Justice from threatening election officials with criminal prosecution over noncitizen‑voting claims. The order, signed by U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson, was issued in response to a lawsuit filed by unions representing California election workers.
summary: A California federal judge Friday ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening election officials with criminal prosecution in its ongoing efforts to crack down on noncitizen voting. U.
author: The Hill

title: Prime Minister Burnham open to slavery apology but rejects reparations
content: The prime minister says Britain must "face up to the past" for its role in the transatlantic slave trade but reparations are "not the right answer".
summary: Prime Minister Burnham open to slavery apology but rejects reparations.
author: BBC Politics

title: Study finds 1 in 4 Americans exaggerate symptoms to obtain antibiotics
content: A new study reports that more than one‑quarter of Americans have exaggerated or fabricated symptoms to obtain antibiotics from their doctors, whether for themselves or their children. The nationwide survey, which included nearly 1,000 respondents, identified common reasons for this behavior, such as feeling very ill or needing to return to work or school.
summary: A new study found that more than a quarter of Americans have exaggerated or fabricated symptoms to obtain antibiotics for themselves or their children. The nationwide survey of nearly 1,000 respondents identified motivations such as feeling very sick or needing to return to work or school.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Hospitalized patients have lower death and readmission rates with female doctors
content: A new ICES study led by a University of Toronto researcher found that hospitalized patients treated by female physicians were less likely to die or be readmitted than those cared for by male physicians. The findings suggest that care by female physicians may be linked to better short‑ and long‑term outcomes for patients with common medical diagnoses.
summary: Study: Hospitalized patients have lower death and readmission rates with female doctors.
author: Medical Xpress

title: CDK1 activity linked to breast cancer resistance to targeted therapy
content: Researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have found that the activity of the protein CDK1 in breast cancers is linked to how the tumors respond to a common targeted therapy. The observation suggests the protein could help guide more personalized treatment decisions for patients.
summary: Researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research found that the activity of the protein CDK1 in breast cancers is linked to how the tumors respond to a common targeted therapy. The insight may help guide more personalized treatment approaches for patients.
author: Medical Xpress

title: People with HIV lose more years of life to smoking than to HIV
content: People with HIV are now losing more years of life to smoking than to the virus itself. Approximately 1.2 million Americans live with HIV, and while smoking prevalence among U.S. adults has dropped below 10% for the first time, the rate among those with HIV remains up to four times higher. Although many individuals with HIV express a desire to quit, their quit‑rate is considerably lower than that of the general population.
summary: People with HIV now lose more years of life to smoking than to HIV itself. About 1.2 million Americans are living with HIV, and while smoking among U.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UT study finds personal life stories aid recovery for personality disorder patients
content: University of Texas research indicates that personal life stories can aid both treatment and personal recovery. The study emphasizes asking individuals about their identity, influences, and future outlook, noting that these questions may be especially significant for people with personality disorders. Clinical psychologist and psychotherapist Silvia Pol’s Ph.D. research finds that focusing on personal narratives can help guide treatment decisions and support recovery processes.
summary: UT research shows how personal life stories can support treatment and personal recovery. Who are you, what has shaped you, and how do you see your future?
author: Medical Xpress

title: European researchers launch ten‑marker personalized score to gauge disease risk and aging
content:
Approximately 60 % of people older than 65 now live with two or more chronic conditions, according to studies conducted in several countries. This high prevalence of multimorbidity has prompted a focus on reversing the trend and encouraging healthier aging.

In response, European researchers have developed a new personalized indicator that uses ten blood markers to flag disease risk and assess healthy aging. By analyzing, with high precision, the chemicals the body produces to function, the score provides a detailed snapshot of a patient’s metabolism and aims to guide interventions that promote long‑term health.
summary: Studies in various countries indicate that about 60% of people over age 65 have two or more chronic conditions. European researchers have created a new personalized indicator that uses ten blood markers to precisely analyze metabolic chemicals and provide a detailed snapshot of disease risk and healthy aging.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Transcription systems influence chromatin dynamics in distinct nuclear regions
content:
DNA in the cell nucleus is packaged into nucleosomes, which are further assembled into chromatin. Traditionally, chromatin is divided into transcriptionally active euchromatin and relatively inactive heterochromatin.  

Recent observations show that nucleosomes are not static; they continuously move within the nucleus. This dynamic motion is closely linked to the physical organization of the genome and its functional state.
summary: DNA is wrapped around histone proteins to form nucleosomes that organize into chromatin, which is divided into transcriptionally active euchromatin and relatively inactive heterochromatin. Nucleosomes continuously move within the nucleus, and this motion is closely related to the physical organization and function of the genome.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds pay‑to‑quit bonuses increase employee effort
content: Researchers from the University of Waterloo, Wilfrid Laurier University, and McMaster University tested pay‑to‑quit programs. Their study confirmed that offering employees money to leave results in those who refuse to quit working harder. The research also uncovered an unexpected benefit that had not been anticipated.
summary: Researchers at the University of Waterloo, Wilfrid Laurier University and McMaster University tested pay‑to‑quit programs. Their results showed that employees who declined the quit money worked harder, confirming the programs work and revealing an unexpected benefit.
author: Phys.org

title: Microquasar Jets Linked to Gamma-ray Binary's Gas Trail Outside Milky Way
content: In 2016 astronomers identified a binary star system in the nearby galaxy that emits unusually strong gamma‑rays. New observations have revealed a trail of cool molecular gas that appears to trace jets from a microquasar, one of the few such objects known outside the Milky Way, suggesting the jets are the source of the gamma‑ray emission.
summary: In 2016, a binary star system emitting unusually strong gamma rays was discovered in our galactic neighborhood. Astronomers have found a trail of cool molecular gas that suggests jets from a microquasar—one of the few known outside the Milky Way—are responsible.
author: Phys.org

title: Crop diversification tested in Rio Grande do Sul improves resilience and yields
content: Researchers at the Center for Carbon Research in Tropical Agriculture (CCARBON) of the University of São Paulo tested a diversification approach in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The study found that varying crop rotations and maintaining continuous vegetation cover on the soil helped shield crops from droughts and floods while also raising overall productivity.
summary: Varying crop rotations and keeping soil continuously covered with vegetation help protect crops against droughts and floods while boosting productivity. The technique was tested in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, by researchers from the Center for Carbon Research in Tropical Agriculture (CCARBON) at the University of São Paulo.
author: Phys.org

title: UTe₂ shows two superconductivity flavors under extreme pressure
content: UTe₂ under extreme pressure displays two distinct “flavors” of superconductivity, according to recent research. Quantum researchers are searching for a topological superconductor—a material that would enable major advances in quantum computing by combining those two superconducting flavors.
summary: UTe₂ exhibits two distinct flavors of superconductivity when subjected to extreme pressure. Quantum researchers are searching for a topological superconductor that could enable major advances in quantum computing by combining such flavors.
author: Phys.org

title: Study maps human urogenital organ development, shows coordinated signaling
content: A recent study mapped human urogenital development within its native spatial context. The research shows that neighboring organs coordinate their growth through cellular communication and molecular signaling during embryogenesis, providing new insight into the co‑development of these structures.
summary: A new study has mapped human urogenital development in its native spatial context. The mapping reveals that neighboring organs coordinate their development through cellular communication and molecular signaling during embryogenesis.
author: Phys.org

title: APOD shows Earth’s night over Iceland’s Hverir with green aurora
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 31 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Night on a Spooky Planet Explanation: What spooky planet is this? Planet Earth on a dark and stormy night, of course. The ghostly scene was photographed at Hverir, a geothermally active area found along northeastern Iceland’s volcanic landscape. Triggered by solar activity, geomagnetic storms have unleashed energetic particles trapped in Earth’s magnetic field. Penetrating the planet’s upper atmosphere at high latitudes, the particles create auroral displays in the starry night sky. Ghostly towers of steam and gas are venting from local fumaroles to dance against the eerie, greenish northern lights. For now, auroral activity on planet Earth remains in a high state as the Sun is only in early phases of decline from the peak of its solar activity cycle. author: NASA News

title: Scribd reports security incident exposing email and partial credit‑card data
content:
Scribd, Inc., the parent company of Scribd, Slideshare, Everand and Fable, disclosed a security incident in a notice sent on Monday, 26 October 2026. The notice, issued by the company’s notification partner Epiq, states that an unauthorized third party may have accessed certain user data stored in one of Scribd’s systems.

According to the notice, the compromised information includes the user’s email address, the last four digits of their credit‑card number, country, credit‑card issuer, credit‑card expiry date and payment history (excluding full card details). Scribd reports no evidence that the data has been misused, but it is informing affected users as a precaution.

The company urges users to remain vigilant for phishing attempts that may impersonate Scribd, Slideshare, Everand or Fable, emphasizing that it will never request usernames, passwords or other sensitive information via email or text. Recipients are advised not to click links in suspicious messages and to access Scribd services directly through official web addresses or by calling the dedicated help line at +1‑877‑361‑9887 during Monday‑Friday hours of 11:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Central European Time.

Scribd says it has secured the affected system, terminated the unauthorized access, and notified law enforcement as well as relevant data‑protection authorities. The company is also working with an expert third‑party cybersecurity firm to strengthen access controls and monitoring, and it references guidance from the National Cyber Security Center on avoiding phishing scams.
summary: Scribd reports security incident exposing email and partial credit‑card data.
author: Hacker News

title: Iranian novelist, British children's author and Azerbaijani writer bridge cultures
content: An Iranian novelist who explores women’s lives, a British children’s author who creates imaginary worlds, and an Azerbaijani writer who works to preserve her country’s cultural identity are linked by stories that travel beyond Baku’s borders, connecting continents and blending cultures through books.
summary: An Iranian novelist explores women's lives, a British children's author creates imaginary worlds, and an Azerbaijani writer works to preserve her country's cultural identity. Their stories cross borders, connect continents, and blend cultures through books.
author: Euronews

title: Syrian curriculum revisions edit images, add hijabs, remove women's photos and statues
content: Syrian curriculum revisions have prompted debate over the removal of images and historical figures. The updates go beyond textual edits, with photos and illustrations altered in Photoshop to add hijabs or long robes to female depictions, delete women’s pictures, and cover or replace statues, sculptures and other artworks.
summary: Changes to the Syrian curriculum included editing images and illustrations in Photoshop. The edits added hijabs or long robes to female figures, deleted women's photos, and covered or replaced statues, sculptures and artworks.
author: Euronews

title: Zelenskyy thanks US for 500 Patriot missile deal, warns delivery may take years
content: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked the United States for a deal to provide 500 Patriot missiles, noting that the weapons may not arrive for several years. He reiterated Kyiv’s longstanding request for additional interceptors to protect its forces from Russian missile and drone attacks, a need that is becoming more urgent as winter approaches.
summary: Zelenskyy thanked the United States for a deal to provide 500 Patriot missiles and said delivery could take years. Kyiv has long called for more interceptors to help its forces fend off Russian missile and drone attacks as winter approaches.
author: Euronews

title: Kärcher CEO calls for less regulation and action to boost Germany, Europe
content: Kärcher, the pressure‑washer maker, reported €3.5 billion in sales for 2025 and employs 17,000 staff worldwide. Its chief executive described a “perfect storm” facing the market and urged a “fitness plan” for Germany and Europe, calling for less regulation and more action to restore economic health.
summary: Kärcher, known for its pressure washers, posted €3.5 billion in sales in 2025 and employs 17,000 people worldwide. Its CEO warned of a 'perfect storm' and urged a fitness plan with less regulation and more action for Germany and Europe.
author: Euronews

title: France deploys 70,000 police as Yellow Vest protests return for “Act III – Halloween”
content: France braces for another weekend of unrest as the Yellow Vests return to the streets under the rallying cry of ‘Act III – Halloween’, with 70,000 police and security forces deployed after the riots and looting of recent weeks. A cash-strapped government faces mounting grievances, a rolling protest movement and little room for manoeuvre ahead of elections, as it struggles to restore order while grappling with crippling debt.
summary: The Yellow Vest movement resumed protests under the banner “Act III – Halloween”. About 70,000 police and security forces were deployed as a cash‑strapped government confronts unrest ahead of elections.
author: France 24

title: France's top court blocks central Paris protest route, allows outskirts path
content:
France’s top court on Saturday overturned a Paris court ruling that had authorized a protest route running from the Bastille to Place de la Nation in the city centre. The court’s decision limits the rally to a route that now passes through the outskirts of Paris instead of the capital’s heart.

Authorities have tightened security and warned that rioters may use Halloween masks to hide their identities. The live blog continues to provide updates on the evolving situation.
summary: France's top court overturned a Paris court decision that had authorized a protest route from Bastille to Place de la Nation in central Paris. The approved route now runs through the outskirts of Paris, and authorities have tightened security amid warnings of rioters using Halloween masks.
author: France 24

title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he fled Brazil to US citing persecution in video
content: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro posted a video message on social media late Friday to declare he fled to the US because he was a victim of 'persecution'. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's election runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, gave no details of how he left the country.
summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, Brazil's defeated right‑wing presidential candidate, posted a video message on social media late Friday saying he fled to the US because he was a victim of persecution. He gave no details of how he left the country after losing the runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
author: France 24

title: France prepares for Halloween protests, shops board up storefronts
content: France prepared for a third weekend of protests that fell on Halloween, with shops boarding up storefronts as authorities worked to avoid a repeat of the street violence that had spread across the country two weeks earlier.
summary: France braced for a third weekend of protests that coincided with Halloween. Shops boarded up and authorities scrambled to prevent a repeat of the street violence that swept the country two weeks ago.
author: France 24

title: Avanti West Coast Pays Over £20m in Passenger Refunds This Summer
content:
Avanti West Coast has paid more than £20 million in passenger refunds for disrupted journeys during the summer months, according to the operator’s latest financial disclosures. The intercity train company’s compensation bill is expected to exceed £70 million for the current financial year, reflecting a rise in claims across its network.

In the period leading up to 25 July, Avanti West Coast disbursed £9.3 million in refunds—almost equal to the company’s annual profits for each of the two preceding years. An additional £12.2 million was paid out over the following eight weeks.
summary: Avanti West Coast Pays Over £20m in Passenger Refunds This Summer.
author: Guardian World

title: Nigel's chiselled cheekbones highlighted in Reform's 'Reformer' digested by John Crace
content: Editor, agony uncle, crossword compiler – he even interviews himself. Our sketchwriter finds there’s no end to Farage’s talents Welcome to your new super, soaraway Reformer. The paper that aims to take you back to the 1950s with all the stories that the mainstream media don’t want you to read. Free to all patriots. And those who happen to have found a copy on the floor of the bus.
summary: John Crace digests Reform's 'Reformer' which notes Nigel's chiselled cheekbones. The piece describes the paper's editor as an agony uncle, crossword compiler who interviews himself and mentions Farage's talents.
author: Guardian World

title: Week three of Russell Brand rape trial reveals five key observations
content:
Russell Brand’s trial at Southwark Crown Court began with widespread media coverage on 12 October.  The former comedian and presenter faces three charges of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault, all alleged against six women and spanning a decade from 1999.  Brand denies all charges, and his wife gave evidence in the case.

The article outlines five observations that emerged during the third week of the trial, summarizing what was learned from the proceedings to date.
summary: The former comedian Russell Brand and his wife testified in the third week of his trial at Southwark Crown Court, which began on 12 October. Brand denies three rape charges, three sexual‑assault charges and one attempted indecent‑assault charge involving six women spanning ten years from 1999.
author: Guardian World

title: Zelenskyy lauds US $2.1bn Patriot missile sale, warns deliveries may take years
content:
The United States has approved a sale of 500 Patriot PAC‑3 missiles to Ukraine, valued at an estimated $2.1 billion. Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, described the decision as strong but cautioned that the delivery of the missiles could take years, emphasizing that stockpiles are needed now to counter Russian ballistic‑missile attacks.

In a statement released on Friday, the U.S. State Department said the proposed sale will improve Ukraine’s capability to meet current and future threats by enhancing its integrated air and missile‑defense systems.
summary: The United States approved a sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine valued at about $2.1 billion. Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised the decision but warned that deliveries could take years and that stockpiles are needed now to counter Russian ballistic missile attacks.
author: Guardian World

title: Riot police confront protesters at Poland's constitutional court after judge suspension
content:
Riot police were deployed to the Constitutional Court in Warsaw on Friday night, where they faced a tense standoff with protesters. President Karol Nawrocki was seen struggling to gain entry to the court building amid the confrontation.  

The police presence followed a decision by a group of government‑appointed judges to suspend the court’s president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański. The suspensions occurred as part of a decade‑long dispute over the court’s legal status and legitimacy.
summary: Riot police confront protesters at Poland's constitutional court after judge suspension.
author: Guardian World

title: Mouria coffeehouse in Exarchia closes after 44 years as lease not renewed
content:
Mouria coffeehouse in Athens’ Exarchia neighborhood has closed after its lease could not be renewed. The historic café, long associated with left‑wing solidarity, resistance, and radicalism, has served as a gathering place for writers, artists, poets, politicians, doctors, lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries for as long as anyone can remember.  

For 44 years, proprietor Christos Vanas—formerly a waiter—has opened the café each morning at 7 a.m. before having his first coffee, welcoming the diverse community that has made Mouria a symbol of the area’s countercultural heritage. The café’s closure marks the end of an era in a neighborhood that is rapidly gentrifying.
summary: Mouria coffeehouse in the Exarchia neighbourhood of Athens could not renew its lease and is closing. The cafe, run by proprietor Christos Vanas for 44 years, has long been a gathering place for writers, artists, poets, politicians, doctors, lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries.
author: Guardian World

title: Albanese to meet King Charles at Commonwealth summit as interest‑rate hike looms
content: The prime minister will speak with King Charles and others at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua and Barbuda Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast As “summit season” begins, reaffirming ties with fellow leaders on the world stage could be a circuit breaker for Anthony Albanese amid domestic and economic woes, analysts have said. But a likely interest rate hike, triggered by higher-than-expected inflation, while the prime minister is overseas will make his job – and the treasurer’s – even harder. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
summary: Prime Minister Albanese will speak with King Charles and other leaders at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua and Barbuda. Analysts say a likely interest‑rate hike triggered by higher‑than‑expected inflation could make his job and the treasurer’s harder while he is overseas.
author: Guardian World

title: Storm warnings issued for Melbourne, Canberra, Sydney and Brisbane as cold front hits
content: Storm warnings have been issued for Melbourne, Canberra, Sydney and Brisbane as a severe cold front moves across Australia’s east and south‑east. The Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) predicts hail, damaging winds and possible flash flooding across Victoria, New South Wales and parts of Queensland into Sunday. Heavy rain, strong winds and thunderstorms are forecast to affect Melbourne and eastern Victoria on Saturday afternoon as the cold front meets warm, humid air. The alerts cover multiple capital cities as the system sweeps the region.
summary: BoM predicts hail, damaging winds and possible flash flooding across Victoria, NSW and parts of Queensland into Sunday. Storm warnings have been issued for Melbourne, Canberra, Sydney and Brisbane as heavy rain, winds and thunderstorms are forecast for Melbourne and eastern Victoria on Saturday afternoon.
author: Guardian World

title: Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86, colleagues post tributes
content: As we all begin to absorb the bitter news of Patrick Stewart's death at the age of 86, a flood of personal tributes are pouring in, reflecting this global treasure's wonderful life lived with a dignity and bravado that few mortals possess. We’re getting just a hint of what Patrick Stewart meant to those who worked with him or knew him throughout his stellar career. Whether on stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company, on TV as the dashing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation," and in Hollywood spectacles like 1984's "Dune," four " Star Trek " feature films, and the many "X-Men" movies in which he portrayed Professor Charles Xavier, Stewart was always the consummate professional. His final screen performance arrives on Dec. 18 with "Avengers: Doomsday" where he’ll present his Charles Xavier character once more. "Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end," Ian McKellen wrote on Instagram of his "X-Men" co-star and friend. "You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love." Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellan in 2000's "X-Men." (Image credit: 20th Century Studios) William Shatner, a fellow Enterprise captain, offered his profound sense of loss on Stewart's passing. The legends shared the screen in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." "What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner posted on Facebook. "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed." Patrick Stewart and William Shatner star in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." (Image credit: Paramount) Akiva Goldsman, co-creator of Paramount+'s " Star Trek: Picard " and "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," delivered a sorrowful message in the aftermath of Stewart's death "Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman wrote. "Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of 'Star Trek' without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more." Stewart's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" family shared their grief and offered up poignant words to try to describe what effect he had on their lives and profession. "There's no one on this planet that I have acted with or directed more often than my late great friend Patrick Stewart," revealed actor and director Jonathan Frakes, who co-starred for over 35 years with Stewart as Commander Will Riker, in a touching statement. "He will be with me forever. May he rest in Peace." Jonathan Frakes and Patrick Stewart share a laugh in "Star Trek: The Next Generation." (Image credit: Paramount) Finally, Marina Sirtis posted a teary-eyed video in which she explained how much of an impact Stewart had on her life during their time together on "The Next Generation" series and films, in which she portrayed Counselor Deanna Troi beside him. "Patrick, I loved you with all my heart," she said on Instagram. "I know you're up there now, reunited with all those that you've loved. But to say that you'll be missed down here is probably the understatement of the century. It was an honor to work with Patrick. It was more than an honor; it was the privilege of my life to work with him."
summary: Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86, colleagues post tributes.
author: Space.com

title: Exeter’s Tom Hooper: ‘Sometimes you’ve just got to suck up a little bit of pain’
content:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter has commented on the club’s history of attracting Australian players, noting that many Wallabies have found a "spiritual home" in Exeter. The article highlights a long list of former Australian players who have played for the team, including Dean Mumm, Dave Dennis, Nic White, Scott Sio, Greg Holmes, Julian Salvi, Ben White, Mitch Lees, Lachie Turner, and Len Ikitau. Baxter observed that these players have generally relished their time in the south-west of England, humorously suggesting they "seem to like the pasties and the cider."

While the piece mentions that local surfing opportunities and beaches may contribute to the appeal, Baxter offered an alternative theory regarding the attraction. He suggested that Exeter and Devon are more similar to Australia than other parts of England, citing the region's open spaces and the club's "old-school" character. Baxter stated that Australian players appear to prefer this specific environment. The article title indicates that the featured player, Tom Hooper, also discussed coping with the English weather, the benefits of rehabilitation, and Australia’s chances in the upcoming World Cup.
summary: Chiefs’ latest Wallaby Tom Hooper discusses dealing with English weather, the positive side of rehab, and Australia’s World Cup chances. Exeter’s director of rugby Rob Baxter notes that Australian players often find a spiritual home in the club's old-school environment.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alex de Minaur reaches 350th career win in Vienna quarter-final
content:
Alex de Minaur reached a career milestone at the Vienna Open by recording his 350th tour-level win, becoming the ninth Australian man to achieve this feat. The world No. 10 defeated Matteo Berrettini 7-6 (7-4), 6-2 in the quarter-final of the ATP 500 event held at the Wiener Stadthalle. This victory marks the second consecutive year that de Minaur has beaten the Italian in this tournament stage.

The result secures a semi-final match for de Minaur against Alexander Zverev, who is described in the report as the world No. 1-elect.
summary: Alex de Minaur defeated Matteo Berrettini 7-6 (7-4) 6-2 in the quarter-final of the Vienna Open. This victory marked the 27-year-old's 350th tour-level win and secured a semi-final match against Alexander Zverev.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England crush USA 55-12 to extend 35-year winning streak
content:
England defeated the United States 55-12 in the WXV Global Series, extending a 35-year winning streak against their opponents. The Red Roses secured their 22nd consecutive victory over the USA, a run that dates back to the 1991 Rugby World Cup. Claudia Moloney-MacDonald was a standout performer for England, scoring four tries during the match.

The United States entered the game in strong form, having won five consecutive matches, including victories over Wales and Ireland. Freda Tafuna, the USA’s No 8, had been a notable performer throughout the tournament. However, England managed to contain Tafuna’s influence. Despite contributions from Alev Kelter and Hope Rogers, the hosts lacked the necessary firepower to challenge the world No 1 team, highlighting the gap between the top three sides and the rest of the competition.
summary: England defeated the United States 55-12 to maintain their 35-year winning streak against the USA. The Red Roses secured the victory with four tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Aston Villa to sue Jamie Carragher over 'unacceptable insults'
content: Villa chair announces plan on social media Carragher said club will ‘never be Man United’ Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters. Carragher told Villa fans to “shut the fuck up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job. Villa responded on Friday evening with a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris.
summary: Aston Villa announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his "unacceptable insults" toward the club and its supporters. Carragher told Villa fans to "shut the fuck up" after suggesting Unai Emery should consider the Manchester United job.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Duncan Ferguson cites relief after Glentoran's 1-1 Irish League draw
content: Duncan Ferguson described feeling "relief" following a 1-1 draw in his first match as Glentoran manager. The new boss noted that his initial week involved managing WiFi connectivity and completing homework.
summary: Duncan Ferguson described feeling relief following a 1-1 draw in his first match as Glentoran manager. He noted that his week was filled with WiFi and homework.
author: BBC Sport

title: Man Utd target Barcelona's Fermin Lopez
content: Manchester United are reportedly targeting Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez, while the La Liga club is showing interest in Lisandro Martinez. Additionally, Arsenal are eyeing Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi, according to Saturday's transfer gossip.
summary: Manchester United are targeting Barcelona player Fermin Lopez while Lisandro Martinez attracts interest from the La Liga side. Arsenal are also eyeing Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi.
author: BBC Sport

title: England Red Roses defeat United States to return to winning ways
content: England's Red Roses have returned to winning ways following a victory over the United States. Despite the win, the team has not fully dispelled doubts regarding their status at the top of the women's game.
summary: England's Red Roses have defeated the United States to return to winning ways. The result leaves some doubts over their position at the top of the women's game.
author: BBC Sport

title: El-Sayed to use metal detector if Trump takes lie detector
content: Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed (D) responded to President Trump’s suggestion that he be forced through a metal detector at the U.S. Capitol if elected. Speaking at a campaign rally in Kalamazoo, Mich., El-Sayed stated he would accept the request if Trump agreed to sit for a lie detector.

title: Searle leads Leicester to 22-16 win over Bristol for Prem top spot
content:

The match was described as an error-strewn contest between two teams that started the evening in second and third position. Despite the mistakes, Leicester emerged as the clear winner, scoring four tries to one in the shootout for the league lead.

The performance was highlighted by fly-half Billy Searle, who was named the game’s outstanding player. Searle’s left boot set up all three of his side’s tries and he also landed two conversions, masterfully steering the Tigers to victory. This result followed on from Leicester’s commanding second-half display against Northampton the previous Saturday.

Bristol, who began the night in third, had moments of promise but struggled with possession. The home side was reduced to 13 players during the second quarter after receiving a brace of yellow cards. Ultimately, Bristol coughed up possession too often, allowing Leicester to maintain control and claim the spoils.

title: Sketch Stadium enables AI agents to play Pictionary via Wakeshift SDK
content:
Sketch Stadium is a new platform that allows artificial intelligence agents to play Pictionary. The project was initially developed as a proof-of-concept for delivering push notifications to AI agents but has been released as a standalone demonstration. Users can connect their own agents to the platform or simply observe ongoing games via a provided link.

In the game, agents subscribe to game events and take turns either drawing or guessing clues. The scoring system awards one point for easy clues, two for medium, and three for hard. The developer noted that the initial version allowed agents to draw lines ten at a time to mimic real Pictionary, but this method proved ineffective. The platform now permits agents to use a subset of SVG for drawing, which has improved performance even for lower-cost models.

To integrate an agent, users do not need to create an account; they only need to add the MCP and authorize it. The project serves as a technical demo for Wakeshift, a cross-harness SDK designed to provide push notifications for agents. This tool attaches to an MCP to allow consumers to subscribe to real-time events and uses specific methods per harness to wake dormant agents.

The developer explained that agents often initiate processes with indeterminate completion times, such as continuous integration or waiting for approvals. Currently, there is no consistent method to wake agents via webhook or push notification, forcing reliance on polling or bespoke integrations. The developer previously addressed this challenge with Clawvisor, where long-polling was the best-supported method for recognizing out-of-band approval actions. Wakeshift aims to solve this by providing a simple SDK that upgrades automatically as harnesses adopt MCP events.
summary: The platform allows agents to subscribe to game events and take turns drawing or guessing using a subset of SVG. The project serves as a tech demo for Wakeshift, an SDK designed to provide push notifications for AI agents.
author: Hacker News

title: Demo Shows FlashAttention Kernel Derived from ~25 Lines of SQL Using New SQL Extensions
content:
A developer has shared a demonstration on Hacker News that automatically deduces a FlashAttention kernel using approximately 25 lines of SQL. The SQL code expresses vanilla attention, a feat made possible by three portable SQL extensions currently under development. These extensions include xarray-sql, a library designed to represent petabyte-scale array datasets in the cloud as tables; ddx, a database extension that adds automatic differentiation in the style of JAX to standard SQL; and einfold, a modular query planner for fast tensor contractions.

The project is built on the thesis that separating logical layers in tensor programs from physical layers is both more correct and more scalable. The author suggests that the relational model and algebra offer fresh perspectives on accelerator programming, proposing to formalize the "Bitter Lesson" of machine learning using relational algebra. The post invites interest from those working at the intersection of database theory and ML systems, directing them to a Discord community for further engagement.
summary: An automatic demo derives a FlashAttention kernel from about 25 lines of SQL using three portable SQL extensions: xarray-sql, ddx, and einfold. The authors invite readers to join their Discord community to explore relational algebra for accelerator programming.

title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
content:
A team of scientists led by Yang Liu of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory has identified a third genuinely ancient Martian meteorite, Teghaza 001. Discovered in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, the rock formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. This discovery adds to the limited number of known ancient Martian samples, which previously included Allan Hills 84001 from Antarctica and a rock from northwest Africa known as Black Beauty. The finding provides a new perspective on Mars’ ancient crust, as most other Martian meteorites on Earth are significantly younger, dating to 2.4 billion years or less.

Liu noted that the rarity of old Martian rocks on Earth may be due to the physical conditions required for a rock to leave the planet. A large impact is necessary to launch material into space, but not all rocks can survive such an event. Weak or loose material may fail to cement into a solid rock capable of overcoming Mars’ gravity. Consequently, the impact process itself acts as a natural filter, preventing weaker rocks from reaching Earth.
summary: Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger.

title: DoorDash CEO: AI agents generate only several hundred orders per quarter
content: As AI tools and agents have continued their march across all aspects of digital life, many companies are trying to use LLMs to improve the experience of purchasing goods and services on the Internet. Thus far, though, a vanishingly small number of people seem to be taking advantage of those capabilities, at least when it comes to using the popular food delivery app DoorDash with an outside AI agent. In a third-quarter earnings call Thursday, DoorDash co-founder and CEO Tony Xu responded to an analyst question by noting that "AI agents are generating several hundred orders [on DoorDash] across the time that they've been up and running." In a marked understatement, Xu called this a "very low use case" for a company that handled just shy of 1 billion orders total in the third quarter of 2026 alone. Speaking generally, Xu said he sees the potential for AI agents to be genuinely helpful for "long consideration purchases" and major decisions where agents would be "doing work on your behalf proactively in the background." However, Xu added, "when it comes to a task that's as simple as ordering food, we tend to see that come directly to DoorDash." Read full article Comments
summary: DoorDash co-founder and CEO Tony Xu stated that AI agents have generated only several hundred orders for the platform since their launch. He described this as a very low use case compared to the nearly 1 billion total orders handled in the third quarter of 2026.

This week, Schnell discovered the depths of the problem himself as he resigned from the university after an advisory committee found that he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and in the Washington Post op-ed, even though publishers required such disclosure. Schnell didn't make it especially easy for the committee to investigate his AI use; the report uses the term "insufficient cooperation." He did turn over his Dartmouth laptop, but he did not turn over logs from his personal LLM accounts related to the writings in question. Nor did he agree to meet with the committee. The committee did get access to the Claude enterprise account Schnell had used through Dartmouth, though. This shows him using the LLM as a tool for revising his papers, finding and fixing bugs in code, and editing or generating figures. title: Ars Staff Mourns Sir Patrick Stewart, Who Died at 86 in Los Angeles
content:
Ars staff is mourning the death of Sir Patrick Stewart, the award-winning actor renowned for his roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise. Stewart passed away yesterday at the age of 86. A statement from his representatives announced that he died at his home in Los Angeles while in the care of his wife, Sunny. The statement noted that Stewart had been undergoing a brief journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia, and that he was surrounded by family, friends, live music, and prayer at the time of his passing.

The family described Stewart as having inspired profound emotion through a lifetime of devotion, leaving behind an enduring reminder of his "invincible grace." In lieu of flowers, the family has requested that memorial contributions be directed to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources. This request was shared through the actor’s X account.
summary: Sir Patrick Stewart, age 86, died yesterday at his home in Los Angeles after a brief journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. His representatives requested memorial contributions to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.

title: New World Screwworm Infestation Spreads to Arizona, 74 Animal Cases Reported
content:
The report notes that four dogs and a cat were attacked this week by flesh‑eating screwworms. The New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation has now spread to a third state, Arizona, joining New Mexico and Texas as the only U.S. states plagued by the parasites. Since the flies re‑invaded the country in June, authorities have identified 74 animal cases.

The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals. The resulting maggots, which resemble screws, bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe and sometimes fatal wounds. After feeding, the maggots drop to the ground to develop into adult flies.

The infestation is described as a genuine fright this Halloween, with the maggots festering along the southern border and continuing to threaten pets in the affected states.
summary: New World Screwworm Infestation Spreads to Arizona, 74 Animal Cases Reported.

title: French port strikes may win better conditions, uncertain impact on militarisation
content:
Carys Garland welcomed Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University, to discuss an international dockworkers’ strike that highlights the link between organized labor, technological change and Europe’s expanding military investment.

Foucart said port workers have a strategic position in global supply chains that gives them exceptional leverage, noting, “They know how powerful they are.” He questioned whether they could influence military policy, but expects the leverage to secure concessions on automation and working conditions, adding, “They can get those concessions. And I think they will get them.”
summary: Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University, says the strategic position of French port workers in global supply chains gives them exceptional leverage during the international dockworkers’ strike. title: On this day in space! Oct. 30, 1964: NASA's weird Lunar Landing Research Vehicle takes 1st test flight to help Apollo astronauts land on the moon
content: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing. The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker. During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV. These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. That facility has since been renamed the Armstrong Flight Research Center after Neil Armstrong, who also piloted — and famously crashed — the "Flying Bedstead" before he went to the moon. The first Lunar Landing Research Vehicle is pictured during a test flight at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in California. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Over 60 years ago this LLRV test flight was a critical step toward landing humans on the moon for the first time, a historic moment that both served an important political purpose while also showcasing the result of monumental scientific and technical progress. While images from this test flight might look like the team are having a bit of fun out in the desert, and perhaps they were, it was also deadly serious. The astronauts who signed onto these crewed missions were doing something that had never been attempted. They were putting their lives on the line for this progress, and this testing was a major piece in reassuring them and NASA that lunar landing could be accomplished, and safely. Today, as we return humans to the moon with NASA's Artemis program, we see parallels between testing done over 60 years ago and testing today. Right now, SpaceX and Blue Origin are testing their lunar landers for crewed lunar landings in the near-future. While we have now been to the moon and have safely and successfully landed humans before, these tests remain critical for the safety and success of the missions. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
summary: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing.

title: A Few Good Men review – Aaron Sorkin’s legal drama makes unwelcome return to stage
content:
Aaron Sorkin’s 1989 courtroom drama, A Few Good Men, has returned to the Broadway stage at Lincoln Center’s Vivian Beaumont theater in New York City. The revival features a retooled version of the classic play, which centers on a cocky military attorney defending two young marines who followed an illegal order with fatal results. The production’s reception has been mixed, with critics noting that unconvincing performances and an ill-fitting big stage have made the current iteration feel like a missed opportunity.

The narrative explores the tension between critiquing a hallowed institution and imbuing it with dignity, a theme comparable to how Sorkin’s The West Wing portrayed the Oval Office. The story is set at the US military base at Guantánamo Bay, where a marine has died under troubling circumstances. Colonel Jessep, the hardliner in command, serves as the ultimate enemy to the protagonist, navy lawyer Daniel Kaffee.

The source suggests that audiences seeking crackling drama and sentimentality about the military would be better served by watching the 1992 film adaptation rather than purchasing tickets to the stage production. Directed by Rob Reiner, the movie is described as a clever, old-fashioned crowd pleaser that received an Oscar nomination. It starred Tom Cruise as Kaffee and Jack Nicholson as Jessep, with the film culminating in a classic trial scene featuring the memorable line, “You can’t handle the truth!”
summary: A Few Good Men review – Aaron Sorkin’s legal drama makes unwelcome return to stage.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Sampa the Great: Nu Zamrock review – a full-circle moment for a world-class act
content:
Sampa Tembo, known professionally as Sampa the Great, has released her third album, Nu Zamrock, which is described as a genre-hopping record that meets the moment with charisma and cheek. The project marks a full-circle moment for the world-class act, reflecting her journey after returning to Africa to live and record.

Tembo’s career began in Australia, where she was based between 2013 and 2019. During that period, she achieved significant recognition, becoming the first woman to win an Australian Recording Industry Association award for hip-hop or rap in 2019. She is also noted as the first and only person to win the Australian music prize twice.

Despite her accolades in Australia, Tembo has consistently emphasized her Zambian birth and Botswana upbringing. In a 2022 interview with the Guardian, she explained that she was frequently misidentified as Australian, which compelled her to actively defend Zambian music and culture. She noted that her background in Botswana and the music she heard while growing up there were often overlooked in these discussions.
summary: Sampa the Great: Nu Zamrock review – a full-circle moment for a world-class act.

title: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and X-Men actor, dies at 86
content:
Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. The actor was widely recognized for bringing gravitas and complexity to the screen, particularly through his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise. His Shakespearean training and sonorous voice established him as a unique charismatic force in Hollywood.

Stewart was a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company’s 1970s stage generation and had previously held small screen roles, including an intimidating portrayal of Sejanus in I, Claudius opposite Derek Jacobi. He achieved significant pop culture stardom by securing the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, the leader of the Federation starship USS Enterprise, in Star Trek: The Next Generation. The series, which served as a reboot of the original Star Trek, ran from 1987 to 1994 and spawned four feature films and a subsequent series, Star Trek: Picard.

Colleagues such as William Shatner have paid tribute to Stewart, noting that he stood for the best of humanity. His career demonstrated the commercial potential of British classical training in American cinema and television, showcasing the technique and style of Shakespearean actors within the industry.
summary: Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86, leaving behind a legacy that included iconic roles as Jean-Luc Picard and Charles Xavier. His Shakespearean training and distinctive voice established him as a charismatic force in Hollywood, bridging British classical theater with American pop culture.

title: SCTV: The Canadian Sketch Show That Launched Stars and Influenced The Simpsons
content:
SCTV, short for Second City Television, is described as one of the most influential comedy shows ever created, having launched the careers of Eugene Levy, Catherine O’Hara, and John Candy. The Canadian sketch series, which aired in the 1970s and 1980s, is noted for influencing The Simpsons and maintaining a dedicated following among comedy enthusiasts, even while Saturday Night Live held mainstream popularity in North America. The show was characterized by its weird, dark, and multilayered style, which was considered years ahead of its time.

Dave Thomas, an original cast member and head writer who was present from the start, discussed the show’s unique approach to humor. He recalled that Conan O’Brien once stated he believed the show was written specifically for him because it contained references O’Brien was certain only he understood. Thomas explained that the writers created content at the top of their reference level, with the intention of seeing if the audience would meet them at that intellectual height.
summary: The Canadian sketch show SCTV influenced The Simpsons and launched the careers of actors including Eugene Levy, Catherine O’Hara, and John Candy. Head writer Dave Thomas stated that the show was written at a high reference level, which Conan O’Brien later said felt specifically tailored for him.

title: Study: Wildlife trade involves twice as many species as previously estimated
content:
A study published in Science Advances reveals that the number of plant and animal species involved in the global wildlife trade is more than twice as high as previously estimated. The research indicates that over 100,000 species are currently traded, encompassing illegal smuggling, ornamental sales, and industries including fisheries, timber, and fashion.

The authors warn that significant gaps exist in global assessments of wildlife trade, noting that past estimates have failed to account for recent developments. Specifically, the study highlights the rapid expansion of the online exotic pet trade, where sellers can easily offer to ship spider eggs internationally or facilitate the clandestine transport of reptiles on aircraft.

Millions of Americans have been falling behind on utility bills, forcing difficult choices between paying for energy, food, medicine, and rent. The current situation presents these households with another round of rising costs for gasoline, electricity, and home heating. In response, Wolfe calls on Congress to take action to ensure families can afford to heat their homes before the winter season starts.

title: Iberian copper mines linked to Late Bronze Age trade reaching Scandinavia
content:

The study indicates that copper from these Iberian sites traveled extensive distances, with some material reaching as far as Scandinavia. This finding highlights the region’s potential role in broader Bronze Age trade networks.

Copper is essential for producing bronze, which shaped tools, weapons, and ornaments across Europe. While many Bronze Age mines have been identified, researchers continue to determine which sites were most active at specific times and how far their resources were distributed.

content:

title: NASA Explores Potential Commercial Servicing for Hubble Telescope
content:
NASA issued a Request for Information (RFI) on October 29 to assess industry capabilities for in-space servicing of the Hubble Space Telescope. The agency seeks to identify commercial options that could extend the telescope’s operational life or support its end-of-life procedures. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that Hubble has significant science ahead and that the agency should explore every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible. He emphasized that if innovative and cost-effective methods exist to extend the life of an asset already in orbit, it is a duty to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to investigate them.

The RFI specifically seeks commercial interest in three potential mission profiles: boosting Hubble to a higher altitude to extend its science lifetime, servicing the telescope to enhance its capabilities, or performing a safe, controlled re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere or orbital disposal at the end of its mission. Nicky Fox, associate administrator of the Science Mission Directorate at NASA Headquarters in Washington, noted that Hubble is a national icon that has changed how humanity views the universe for more than 35 years. Fox highlighted the rapid evolution of the commercial industry in offering new capabilities for in-space satellite capture and servicing, stating that NASA is eager to explore possibilities to boost Hubble to a higher orbit while developing the flagship mission to follow.

Technical constraints drive the urgency of these efforts. Like all spacecraft in low Earth orbit, Hubble’s altitude is slowly decreasing due to atmospheric drag because the telescope lacks a propulsion system to maintain its own orbit. Analysis predicts that Hubble is likely to re-enter the atmosphere between 2033 and 2034. Consequently, NASA anticipates that any servicing or boosting mission would need to take place by 2032. The RFI remains open for responses until 3 p.m. EST on Monday, November 30, and is available online.

The Hubble Space Telescope has been operating for more than three decades and continues to make discoveries that shape the fundamental understanding of the universe. It is a project of international cooperation between NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA). NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, manages the telescope and mission operations, with support from Lockheed Martin Space, based in Denver. The Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy, conducts Hubble science operations for NASA.
summary: The Hubble Space Telescope returns to orbit as an improved telescope after its second servicing mission in February 1997. NASA NASA issued a Request for Information Oct.
