title: Hubble Finds Wind From Exploding Stars Blocks Radiation, Challenging Early Universe Theory
content: Astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope have made a discovery that challenges the leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense hydrogen fog roughly 13 billion years ago. Previous scientific consensus held that powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies, thereby clearing the cosmic fog. However, new observations indicate that these winds actually block radiation instead.
summary: Astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope discovered that winds from exploding stars block radiation instead of helping it escape galaxies. This finding challenges the leading explanation that such winds cleared the early universe's dense hydrogen fog about 13 billion years ago.

title: Scientists reveal hidden snakebite crisis killing up to 513,000 people a year
content: A new study estimates that venomous snakebites cause between 274,000 and 513,000 deaths annually, a figure significantly higher than official statistics suggest. Researchers indicate that up to 7 million people may suffer snake envenoming each year. Additionally, the study reports that more than 800,000 survivors are left with long-term disabilities.
summary: A new study estimates that 274,000 to 513,000 people die each year from venomous snakebites worldwide. The study also reports that up to 7 million people suffer snake envenoming annually and over 800,000 survivors experience long‑term disabilities.

title: Scientists find 'sea muppets', seahorse‑like deep‑sea fish never seen alive
content: Scientists have identified three deep-sea fish, nicknamed "sea muppets," as belonging to a distinct evolutionary group despite their seahorse-like appearance. This finding demonstrates that nature evolved this unusual body shape independently. The elusive creatures are known from only seven specimens, and no one has ever observed one alive.
summary: Scientists discovered three deep‑sea fish that resemble seahorses but belong to a separate evolutionary group. The creatures, nicknamed "sea muppets", are known from only seven specimens and have never been observed alive.

title: Study Finds 54% of Young Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Achieve Remission in Six Months
content: A new study indicates that 54% of adults under 45 with type 2 diabetes achieved remission after six months of an intensive low-calorie diet and structured exercise program. This result stands in contrast to the 4% remission rate observed in participants receiving usual care, suggesting the potential efficacy of this combined approach for younger adults.
summary: A new study found that 54% of participants under age 45 with type 2 diabetes achieved remission after six months of an intensive diet and exercise program. Only 4% of participants receiving usual care achieved remission.

title: Computer scientist overcomes 25-year-old network distance calculation limit
content:
A computer scientist has broken a limit that has stood since 1996 by solving a nearly 25‑year‑old problem about calculating distances across huge networks. The new algorithm provides more reliable estimates for closely connected points while maintaining speed, surpassing earlier methods.

The improvement comes from a smarter way of sampling network connections at multiple scales, enabling faster and more accurate distance calculations.
summary: A computer scientist achieved a breakthrough in a nearly 25‑year‑old problem of calculating distances across large networks. The new algorithm provides more reliable estimates for closely connected points while maintaining speed, using a smarter multi‑scale sampling of network connections.

title: Scientists Explain How Crocodiles Survived the Asteroid that Killed Dinosaurs
content: Scientists may have solved a 66‑million‑year‑old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs. A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that the reptiles’ preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that stayed habitable even after the catastrophic impact.
summary: Scientists have analyzed fossils and ancient climates to explain how crocodiles survived the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs. Their preference for warm environments kept them in tropical refuges that remained habitable after the impact.

title: Astronauts complete 7‑hour spacewalk installing new solar array on ISS
content: Two astronauts completed a 7‑hour, 11‑minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station. The installation brings NASA closer to a major power upgrade, and once the final array is installed on November 5, the station will have up to 30 % more available power to support critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.

title: Voyager 1 to Reach One Light‑Day from Sun on Nov 18 2026
content:
November’s Night Sky Notes: Light‑Day Away

In 1977 NASA launched two identical spacecraft, Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, to take advantage of a planetary alignment that occurs once every 175 years. The alignment of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune allowed the twin probes to use six gravity assists to visit each of the four largest planets in the outer solar system. The mission delivered close‑up images and scientific data on the gas and ice giants, including several of their moons.

After completing their encounters with Saturn in the early 1980s, the Voyager probes went their separate ways. Voyager 2 continued toward Uranus and Neptune, while Voyager 1 captured a final portrait of the solar system—excluding Mercury and Mars—including the last image of Earth, the pale blue dot. The Voyager missions set the stage for later orbiter missions such as Galileo to Jupiter and Cassini to Saturn.

Each spacecraft carries a 12‑inch phonograph record known as the Golden Record. The record contains spoken greetings in 55 languages, 27 musical tracks, 116 images, and other sounds from Earth. The outer cover is etched with the Sun’s position relative to 14 pulsars and includes instructions for playback. The record itself is plated with copper and gold, while the cover is made of aluminum and electroplated with an ultra‑pure sample of the isotope uranium‑238, which has a half‑life of 4.468 billion years.

Both Voyager probes crossed the heliopause—the boundary where the Sun’s solar wind meets the interstellar medium—in August 2012 (Voyager 1) and November 2018 (Voyager 2). NASA’s Deep Space Network continues to communicate with the spacecraft and track their positions. At the time of this article, the Canberra antenna was tracking Voyager 1 at a distance of 25.80 billion km, or just over 16 billion miles, from Earth.

On November 18, 2026, 49 years after launch, Voyager 1 will reach the one‑light‑day mark, 16.1 billion miles from the Sun. This milestone highlights the vast distances measured in light‑time units, a concept familiar from science‑fiction and stargazing alike. The Voyager spacecraft remain outside the heliosphere, the protective bubble created by the Sun that extends well beyond Pluto’s orbit.
summary: 2 min read November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away NASA’s Voyager mission took advantage of a once-every-175-year alignment of the outer planets for a grand tour of the solar system. The twin spacecraft revealed details about Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune – using each planet’s gravity to send them on to the next destination.
author: NASA News

title: GLP-1 weight‑loss drugs may worsen rising eating disorder rates
content:
A new report published in JAMA Psychiatry indicates that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa increased by 71% between 1990 and 2023. By 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people were living with one of these two disorders, a figure researchers expect to rise to 21.8 million by 2050. The study, led by Ruhai Bai at the Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University, utilized statistical models to analyze data from 204 countries and territories. The researchers calculated that these conditions cost the world the equivalent of approximately 3.83 million years of healthy life in 2023, measured in disability-adjusted life years.

Clinical experts suggest that environmental factors, including social media and the COVID-19 pandemic, have contributed to this rise. Cynthia Bulik, a clinical psychologist at the University of North Carolina, notes that social media comparisons, influencers, and diet trends serve as precipitating events for eating disorders. Research from the University of Melbourne found that TikTok algorithms delivered 4,343% more “toxic eating disorder videos” to users with these conditions compared to those without. Additionally, data from 2021 showed that hospitalizations for eating disorders in the US doubled between 2018 and 2020, a trend experts link to the social isolation of lockdowns.

Cheri Levinson, a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville, reports seeing more patients with severe symptoms than at any point in her 20-year career. She states that many of these patients are misusing GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, which she describes as a potential trigger for worsening conditions. In a small study published earlier this year, Levinson and colleagues found that 30% of people with eating disorders had used GLP-1 drugs, with 10% appearing to misuse them. Levinson believes this misuse rate is an underestimate and reports cases of children developing eating disorders after being prescribed these medications for medical reasons or purchasing them online.

The accessibility of GLP-1s has increased, with a Gallup survey indicating that 15% of Americans have used these drugs for weight loss. Drug companies are developing new formulations, and versions are available through compound pharmacies or online sources. Bulik expresses concern that GLP-1s may lead to faster and more extreme weight loss in individuals with anorexia nervosa, resulting in patients arriving at treatment in advanced stages of illness that are difficult to reverse. Both Levinson and Bulik are continuing to study the impact of these drugs on eating disorders.

In response to these concerns, Bulik contributed to research and clinical guidelines published earlier this month. These guidelines recommend that doctors screen for eating disorders before prescribing GLP-1s, provide more patient education, and implement robust monitoring for individuals taking the drugs. Levinson adds that she is not surprised if the number of eating disorder cases doubles again, noting that she is currently seeing patients as young as eight and nine years old with the conditions. The true impact of eating disorders is likely higher than reported figures, as anorexia and bulimia represent less than half of all eating disorders, according to Levinson.
summary: A JAMA Psychiatry study reported a 71% increase in the incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa from 1990 to 2023, with an estimated 18.1 million people affected in 2023. Clinical psychologists say that GLP‑1 weight‑loss drugs are being misused by people with eating disorders, potentially worsening symptoms and contributing to earlier onset.

Cleaning up PFAS Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS, or “forever chemicals,” are linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. title: iOS app Oh My Hours tracks wasted Instagram and TikTok time in hour blocks
content: The iOS app Oh My Hours brutally shames users by tracking how many hours they’ve lost to scrolling. It divides each day into hour‑long blocks and highlights the blocks spent on Instagram and TikTok, offering a new approach to curbing screen time.
summary: The iOS app Oh My Hours takes a new approach to curbing screen time. It splits the day into hour‑long blocks and shows which blocks were wasted on Instagram and TikTok.
author: Wired

title: TraderTraitor linked to $6.3 B Binance hack executed in 20 minutes
content: A $6.3 billion hack of Binance was reportedly executed in just 20 minutes. Multiple crypto‑tracing firms have identified the North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor as a possible perpetrator of what they describe as the largest digital heist in history, with billions of cryptocurrency likely unrecoverable.
summary: Multiple crypto‑tracing firms say the North Korean hacker group TraderTraitor may be behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack. The breach reportedly took only 20 minutes and is described as the largest digital heist in history, with billions of crypto likely gone for good.
author: Wired

title: Wikimedia Foundation warns bad AI copyright ruling could harm open web
content:
The Wikimedia Foundation filed an amicus brief on Friday in a group of landmark lawsuits that pit publishers, including The New York Times, against OpenAI and Microsoft. In the brief, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia argues that courts should legally protect large‑language models that train on copyrighted material while exempting chatbots that merely regurgitate that material to users.  

Wikimedia warns that a strictly black‑and‑white ruling could either strip Wikipedians of useful AI‑based tools or threaten the open web. The foundation takes no side in the litigation but expresses concern that the parties’ positions push for an overbroad approach.
summary: Wikimedia Foundation warns bad AI copyright ruling could harm open web.
author: The Verge

title: Maine Senate race pivots on data center controversy as Collins faces Jackson
content: Maine Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican, was midway through defending her record during the final debate of the midterms when an audience member cut her short. "I'm terrified," a man shouted. "AI data centers are destroying our climate. They are poisoning our water." Collins brushed off the outburst, tying the man to her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson. But the fear echoing through the auditorium wasn't so easily dismissed. Just days before voters head to the polls, the rapid expansion of resource-hungry data centers has exploded into one of Maine's most volatile campaign issues. Maine drew national headlines in April when the state Le …
summary: During the final midterm debate, Republican Sen. Susan Collins was interrupted by a protester who warned that AI data centers are destroying the climate and poisoning water. Collins brushed off the outburst, tying the protester to her Democratic challenger Troy Jackson as the data center issue becomes a volatile campaign topic.
author: The Verge

title: Binance Reports $6.3 Billion Crypto Theft, Claims to Cover Losses
content:
Binance announced that $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency has been stolen from its platform, a theft that is believed to be the largest hack in the history of digital assets. The exchange has stated that the loss is the result of a coordinated cyberattack and that the incident represents a record‑breaking breach.

In a series of updates posted to X, Binance confirmed that user funds remain safe and that roughly $3 billion of the impacted assets have already been frozen. The company has pledged to cover any losses incurred by users as a result of the hack.

Binance also disclosed that it has an emergency reserve fund of about $1.3 billion, based on its last valuation, to protect user assets in such situations. Additionally, the company has set aside more than $6.34 billion of its own funds to cover the incident, with $5 billion of those funds earmarked for this purpose.
summary: Binance says it will cover all loses resulting from the hack. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Turbosquid Binance has disclosed that $6.3 billion worth of crypto funds have been stolen from the platform, in what's believed to be the biggest cryptocurrency hack on record.
author: The Verge

title: Apple releases touchscreen MacBook Pro featuring PROLED XDR OLED display
content: Touch ‘em if you got ‘em. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Apple's long-awaited touchscreen MacBook Pro is finally here. I got to try this MacBook that, according to the last two Apple CEOs, shouldn't exist. The most surprising thing is how normal it is. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display (what a name) has one of the nicest screens I've seen on a laptop. The current Mini LED MacBook Pros are great, but the OLED has those even inkier blacks. It also gets super bright, with incredibly rich colors and infinite contrast. Apple calls it a "reference-caliber display," which is a very Apple-y marketing term, but it walks the walk by being the first laptop display with support for Apple CMF 2026 color …
summary: Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro, called the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, is now available. Reviewers note its OLED screen delivers inkier blacks, high brightness, rich colors, infinite contrast, and is the first laptop display to support Apple CMF 2026 color.

title: Apple Pencil makes Apple Duo a practical notebook substitute
content: If not notebook, why notebook shaped? Apple's $2,000 folding phone is a surprisingly good stand-in for a $20 notebook. Believe me; nothing gets me going quite like a new notebook. This one will be different, I think. This time, I really will take it everywhere. Inspiration can strike at any moment, and you have to be ready, says David Sedaris in that one MasterClass I watched on a flight. With this one special new notebook, I will see the world differently. I'll steal moments for myself to write, rather than pulling out my phone to scroll at every opportunity like a trained monkey. And a few weeks, a month, or maybe a year later, I'll concede that it didn't change everything an …
summary: The author describes the $2,000 Apple Duo folding phone as a surprisingly good stand‑in for a $20 notebook when paired with the Apple Pencil. They plan to carry it everywhere to write instead of scrolling on their phone.

title: Apple HomeView and Amazon Echo Show 16 poised as family computers
content: Three years ago, I wrote an obituary for the smart display. The category - smart speakers with touchscreens attached - was stuck with a few underpowered gadgets from Google and Amazon that tried to do too much and did too little well. Back then, I also laid out what they needed to do to improve. This month, Apple and Amazon launched new smart displays that check nearly every box on that list. Based on my brief hands-on time with Apple's first smart display, the $299 HomeView, and Amazon's $499.99 Echo Show 16, a ground-up rebuild of its smart display line, these could finally turn the smart display into what it should have been all along: …
summary: Apple and Amazon have launched new smart displays that meet most of the improvements the author previously outlined. After brief hands‑on testing of Apple’s $299 HomeView and Amazon’s $499.99 Echo Show 16, the author says they could finally fulfill the smart‑display role as a family computer.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says AI math output will continue despite mathematicians' concerns
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the company’s recent flood of AI‑generated mathematical results and expressed sympathy for researchers who are trying to keep up. In a Thursday episode of the Cheeky Pint podcast, he said, “I think, on net, the world deserves to understand how the universe works,” while adding, “But I do have empathy for the method.”  

Altman made clear that OpenAI will not pause its output and hinted that more discoveries may follow from the company’s growing stockpile. His remarks are among the first public statements in which the OpenAI chief directly addressed the impact of the firm’s work on the mathematics community.
summary: Sam Altman, OpenAI CEO, said he sympathizes with mathematicians overwhelmed by the company's AI-generated results. He told the Cheeky Pint podcast released Thursday that OpenAI will not stop the math onslaught and may release more discoveries.
author: The Verge

title: Anthropic files 335-page S-1 prospectus, urging investors to believe in transformative AI
content: Investing in any stock is kind of like gambling in the sense that you're betting your money on a company's future performance. But how do you bet on a technology that could, in the worst-case scenario, "pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," or best case, "bring forth an age of miracles"? To some extent, Anthropic suggests in a letter at the top of its S-1 filing, you have to just believe. Anthropic's 335-page S-1 prospectus, filed Monday, is part of a steady hype escalation in Silicon Valley's interactions with Wall Street. In some ways, it's not even that bizarre; SpaceX IPO'd in June after filing an S-1 that referenced din …
summary: Anthropic's 335-page S-1 prospectus, filed Monday, contains a letter telling investors they must simply believe in the technology. The filing reflects a hype escalation in Silicon Valley's ties to Wall Street, exemplified by SpaceX's June IPO after its own S-1 filing.
author: The Verge

title: Cowboy Space reveals specifications for its Big Iron medium‑lift rocket
content: Welcome to Edition 9.17 of the Rocket Report! It's been a while since an American company announced plans for a medium-lift new launch vehicle, but that's what happened this week when a startup named Cowboy Space revealed specs for its Big Iron rocket, named for the classic country-western song by Marty Robbins. I'm a huge fan of the name. Maybe Cowboy Space is striking while the iron is hot as the space industry frets over demand for launch outpacing supply. However, Cowboy Space lags far behind so many other launch providers nearing the launch pad with their medium-class rockets, and the company didn't have much hardware to show at this week's big reveal. In other words, don't mistake style for substance. But we're rocket fans at Ars, and we wish them luck. As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar. Virgin's new rocket plane reaches home port. The first of Virgin Galactic's new Delta-class rocket planes left its Arizona factory Wednesday for a trip to Spaceport America in neighboring New Mexico, where it will undergo preparations for a test campaign culminating in suborbital flights to the edge of space, Ars reports. Virgin Galactic expects the craft's first commercial spaceflight to take place "early" in the second quarter of 2027, but like every other projected date in aerospace, this should be taken with a grain of salt. Virgin Galactic halted commercial flights of its previous vehicle, VSS Unity, in 2024. Read full article Comments

title: Film “You Can See Everything” portrays Elizabeth Holmes’ final days before prison
content:
In 2015, Elizabeth Holmes was celebrated as Silicon Valley’s youngest and richest self‑made female billionaire, with her company Theranos valued at $9 billion. The company’s reputation collapsed after accusations of fraud regarding its blood‑testing device, leading to a high‑profile trial. Holmes was convicted on four counts and sentenced to 11 years in prison.

The former entrepreneur has returned to the headlines with the film You Can See Everything, which portrays the final days before Holmes entered prison after exhausting her appeals. The movie is co‑directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim and has been described as a surreal, absurdist piece that has generated widespread enthusiasm and hype, with some calling it the best film of the year.

Critics, however, have offered counter‑views. The reviewer notes that while the film contains entertaining moments—particularly in its second half—it delivers little new insight into Holmes or the Theranos saga. The film is described as shallow, running in circles, and not justifying the intense hype surrounding it.
summary: The documentary, co‑directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, depicts the period just before Elizabeth Holmes began her 11‑year sentence after being convicted on four fraud counts. The reviewer calls the film shallow and lacking fresh insight despite its hype.
author: Ars Technica

title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid launches with 1.5‑L series e‑Power system
content:
Nissan supplied a flight from Washington, DC, to Santa Barbara, California, and lodging so that Ars could test‑drive the company’s new 2027 Rogue Hybrid. The outlet notes that it does not accept paid editorial content.

The 2027 model is the latest iteration of Nissan’s best‑selling Rogue SUV and is being introduced with the newest version of the brand’s e‑Power hybrid system, which Ars evaluated in February. Unlike most current hybrids that operate as parallel systems—using an internal‑combustion engine and an electric motor together to drive the wheels—Nissan’s e‑Power uses a series‑hybrid layout. In this configuration the gasoline engine functions solely as a generator to charge the traction battery, while the electric motor provides propulsion.

Under the hood, the Rogue Hybrid is equipped with a 1.5‑liter, three‑cylinder turbocharged direct‑injection engine that produces 148 hp (110 kW). The engine is limited to 5,200 rpm and is tuned primarily to charge the battery rather than to handle direct drivetrain loads. This design enables a reported thermal efficiency of 42 percent, a figure the article compares only to Formula 1 power units.

Visually, the vehicle features a crisp shut line and slim horizontal headlights that the writer likens to a Range Rover aesthetic. These details, combined with the series‑hybrid powertrain, define the 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid as a model that aims to deliver electric‑vehicle‑like driving dynamics without requiring external charging.
summary: Nissan introduced the 2027 Rogue Hybrid, the latest version of its best‑selling Rogue SUV equipped with the e‑Power series‑hybrid system. It is powered by a 1.5‑liter three‑cylinder turbocharged engine that produces 148 hp (110 kW), revs to 5,200 rpm to charge the traction battery, and achieves roughly 42 % thermal efficiency.
author: Ars Technica
